correctness.rationale: PASS. For W_{m+1}=K_1 join C_m with m>=4, doubled centered vertices equal indegree minus outdegree. Hub degree m and rim degree 3 give the exact identity 4R^2=(2k-m)^2+m+8s, k hub-indegree, s whole-wheel rim sources or sinks. Spoke/rim binary words forbid a directed triangle at each unequal spoke junction; for mixed spoke words any longer hub cycle would cross an oppositely oriented boundary, and uniform spokes leave just four directed full-rim words to remove. Consequently the stated fixed four-state cyclic transfer M yields F_m(u,v)=tr M^m-2(1+u^m), and F_m(1,1)=3^m-3. Splitting mixed spoke words into runs forces at least one rim source/sink per alternating run and exactly one of each iff one one-run and one zero-run; there are m*k*(m-k) such words for 1<=k<m. Minimization of (2k-m)^2 with s=2, then comparison to unmixed endpoints, gives exact parity first-shell values and counts. Independently enumerated every 2^(2m) orientation m=4,5,6,7 with Kahn DAG test, verifying all count and first-shell values. General proof is combinatorial, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: PASS, bounded. The full public wheel acyclic-orientation flip-graph degree-distribution theorem computes how many arcs can flip at each orientation, a different invariant from Euclidean half-signed-degree norm; it cannot recover the source/sink rim statistic and radius polynomial without extra work. The complete universal cone/farthest graphical-zonotope theorem computes maximum radius (for W_{m+1} as a join) but not minimum over vertices or joint k,s distribution. The Mühlherr–Poullot 2026 acyclic-polynomial primary abstract treats AO graph Hamiltonicity, and full manuscript could not be obtained through the tested open sources; its possible hidden radial invariant is a bounded priority risk. Classical count 3^m-3 and orientation bijection are credited, not novel.
